resistance-selection.alt: Four panels of 16 insects. Generation 0, before spraying: 1 of 16 carries a resistance allele. Spraying: 14 are killed and 2 survive, the resistant insect and one susceptible insect. Generation 1, offspring of the survivors: 7 of 16 are resistant. Generation 6, after years of spraying: 15 of 16 are resistant. The key notes that the resistance allele was present before any spraying.

arms-race.alt: A cycle of four steps. 1: Newts carry a nerve toxin; snakes without resistance that eat one are paralyzed or die. 2: Snakes with resistant sodium channels survive and leave more offspring. 3: Resistance becomes common in the snake population, and low-toxin newts get eaten. 4: Newts with more toxin survive attacks and leave more offspring, leading back to step 1. Center text: each side is the other side's selective pressure.
